name: @kruddage/workspace
//version: 0.0.0 is inert and deliberate, not a stale placeholder. version.txt at the repo root is the single source of the released version; introspect.scm stamps it into the WASM build and the shell template, and the site's cache-busting hash derives from what that produces, so routing the number through package.json would put Node in the path of a fact the C build needs. See README.md's 'Versioning and releases' and WORKSPACE.md (Q3).
description: pnpm workspace root for the KRUDD engine. The engine itself still builds through kruddmake, which is not in this workspace; this layer sequences the JS packages and enforces the boundaries between them.

scripts.//test: The workspace's own suite: every package's own `test` script (barriers, engine, site, render-diff — dawn-smoke has none, it holds no JS). Pure Node, no compiler, no emsdk — and it does not run the native C suite. That is test:native below, or sh krudd/kruddmake/run-tests.sh directly. See WORKSPACE.md (Q2).
scripts.//test:native: The native C suite (every *_test.c under krudd/engine/), through the workspace's own door. Needs a C compiler and nothing else — see README.md's Prerequisites. This is the same suite sh krudd/kruddmake/run-tests.sh runs; use that path directly on a box with no Node, which is why CI's sanitizer and coverage jobs call it that way rather than through this script. See WORKSPACE.md (Q2).
scripts.//typecheck: Only @kruddage/editor has TypeScript to check, and `pnpm -r` simply finds nothing to do in the packages that do not. It is separate from `test` because it is a different question — `test` asks whether the code works, this asks whether it type-checks — and separate from `build` because the editor's build needs the WASM artifact and this needs nothing. CI runs it in the workspace job, which has no emsdk.
